root_cause_evidence.tool_surface: with this model the client exposes only the code-mode surface: namespaces functions (exec/wait/request_user_input*), clock (sleep), collaboration (spawn_agent/…). The platform MCP server is not offered as its own namespace.
root_cause_evidence.direct_surface_comparison: with a model that has no client-side metadata (the local stub name) the same client offers the MCP server as its own namespace and the tool call succeeds; with this vendor model only the code-mode surface is offered and the model never enters functions.exec for this call
root_cause_evidence.model_behavior: the model chose clock/collaboration tools instead of functions.exec even when the instruction contained the exact one-line JavaScript
root_cause_evidence.rejected_hypothesis: the bridge was connected and its tools were listable via the MCP handshake in all four attempts
instruction_variants_tried: name the server and tool plainly
give the exact one-line functions.exec JavaScript
offer both surfaces in one instruction
tell the model to enumerate Object.keys(tools) and call the matching entry
root_cause_evidence.client_own_contract: the functions.exec description states nested tools are normalized identifiers (e.g. `await tools.mcp__ologs__get_profile(...)`), so our callable would be tools.mcp__agent_weave_probe__task_get
root_cause_evidence.surface_policy: every known model in the operator catalog (gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra) receives the code-mode surface; only an unrecognised model name falls back to exposing the MCP namespace directly, and no real model runs under such a name
